## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `80bc14b0b0af5365e7fce7d13085a390829ab696`
Local-runs: probe — one read-only `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` on this head in a temporary worktree (removed afterwards), to check the replay claim against the tool itself instead of the PR body
Scope: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` + none

Inputs read: card #33848 body and its three comments (triage 6894767153, claim 6897694093, os-dev-report 6898826924); PR #34080 body, file list (2 files, +347 / -7) and net diff against `main` (merge base `e71ecc1b`); the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at this head to judge the diff, never reviewed.

Check-runs on the head at review time: every Lint lane (`Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, both other scoped lanes, the `Lint & Repo Gates` aggregator), all four Type Check lanes, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Test Core (2/8)` completed success. Still running: `Test Core (1/8)`. The rest are skipped by their filters. PR `mergeable_state` reads `blocked`.

Findings: 1 must-fix, 2 should-fix, 4 nits.

### ① Derived judgments

Verified by reading the diff and the head:

- **Transitive.** `importGraphReach` is a breadth-first forward closure from `entry.files` over `loadEdgeTargets`, with a `seen` set (cycles terminate) and a first-importer map; `importGraphChain` walks it back with its own cycle guard. Read from the changed module's side that is the reverse import graph at any depth. The changed path must be under `scripts/pm/`; the walk itself crosses all of `scripts/`, so a gate outside `scripts/pm/` that imports into it, at any depth, is covered.
- **Edge forms.** Static `import … from` and `export … from` (one shared regex), the side-effect form, a literal `import()` and `import(new URL(literal, import.meta.url))` are each read; comments are masked, a keyword in a string or template literal is refused by the `isCode` test, self-test bodies are deliberately not masked. Each form has a fixture row.
- **Unreadable `import()` widens** to every code-position relative module literal in the same file. Confirmed against the live seams: `RECOGNISER_SOURCES` (`./record-recognisers.mjs`, `./check-handover.mjs`), `ARM_READER_SOURCE`, and `loadGovernedRegister` all keep relative literals in the importing file.
- **`gitPathList` reuse.** The diff adds no git reader and no line-split reader at all; the replay row takes a literal two-path list. Nothing to restate.
- **Consulted last, additive.** The new branch is the final statement of `coveringKey`, after the identity, trigger, job-filter, hint and read keys have each returned. It can only turn a `null` into a match; no earlier key's `key` or `via` can change. Additivity holds by construction.
- **Replay.** Probe result on this head for PR #33804's first file list: 62 commands, exit 0, including `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-execute`, `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-validate` and `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch`. The PR's number and its three lines are confirmed. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (which runs the replay row, the transitive row and the two edited rows) is green on this head.
- **Rows.** Transitive row present (fixture `gate.mjs → a.mjs → b.mjs`, through the real `coveringKey`, chain asserted). Ablation-sensitive rows: the PR quotes exactly four rows red with the branch disabled; the ablated blob `7d65b7fe4962` is the blob of `dispatch-gates.mjs` at this head (the diff's index line reads `6343de57..7d65b7fe`), so the ablation ran on the bytes under review even though it predates the merge of `main`. Not re-run here.
- **Forced edits, both forced and both named in the PR body.** (1) The #13126 witness asserted `coveringKey(…) === null` for a module under `scripts/pm/` that `bare-root-worklist.mjs` imports; the new key necessarily answers it. (2) The read-key additivity row strips `entry.reads` and compares; with the new key placed after the read key, the stripped side is answered by the import graph, so the row must strip `importReach` too to keep comparing against the keys consulted before the read key. Neither edit weakens what the row claimed.

**must-fix M1 — an unreadable `import()` whose target is spelled from the repo root is dropped, and that fails toward deriving LESS inside the dispatcher family the card names.** The fallback takes relative literals only. The docblock and the PR body justify refusing root-spelled paths with a claim about the tree: that spelling is "a fixture row or a file a self-test reads as text", and a module loaded by root path "lives in spawned-child templates". Two in-process loads at this head contradict it:

- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` lines 4529 and 4567: the self-test's no-run conformance battery does `await import(pathToFileURL(join(REPO_ROOT, sender)).href)` for every sender it discovers, and names its floor as code-position root-spelled literals (`KNOWN`: `scripts/pm/close-cards.mjs`, `issue-create.mjs`, `issue-transfer.mjs`, `label-write.mjs`, `post-stamped.mjs`, `rerun-failed.mjs`). It then calls each sender's exported relay-miss probe.
- `scripts/pm/check-dispatch-gates.mjs` line 595: `await import(resolve(ROOT, TOOL))` with `TOOL = 'scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs'`.

Consequence for the first: `close-cards.mjs`, `issue-create.mjs` and `issue-transfer.mjs` have no static importer anywhere under `scripts/`, so no import chain reaches them from `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch`; the literals sit inside `selfTest()`, which the hint scan masks; `dispatch.mjs` carries no `dispatch-gates:` declaration; and the family runs unconditionally in CI. So a card editing one of those senders can redden the dispatcher's self-test in CI without that family being derived, which is the card's defect (a self-test that loads a changed `scripts/pm` module) in the family the card's own acceptance line names. This is read from the code, not measured: the one probe was spent on the replay. Required: either take code-position root-spelled first-party module literals as edges when a file has an unread `import()` (the cost the PR measured is five extra modules for `check-governed-merges.mjs`, which is the side this tool is supposed to err on), or show with a live-tree row that an edit to `scripts/pm/issue-create.mjs` places `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch`; and correct the sentence in the docblock and the PR body either way. The fixture row that pins "a root-spelled path is not" an edge moves with it.

**should-fix S1 — the reach is seeded from `entry.files` only, so the import closure of a program a family spawns is not walked.** The PR discloses that a spawned child is not an import edge and says the run key answers it "where it applies". It does not for this card's class: the spawn follow sits below `if (entry.selfTest) continue`, and it contributes population hints, never the child's path or the child's imports. Live shape: `check:pm-dispatch-gates` runs `check-dispatch-gates.mjs`, which spawns `dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test`; that family is derived for the replay paths (probe), through an earlier key, so no live miss is shown. Carrier if not fixed here: a follow-up card on `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, serial after #34002.

**should-fix S2 — the wall-clock price is not stated.** Discovery now scans every reached file once more (`scanSource` over files of 17k and 33k lines). The probe took 48.7 s wall for one `--commands` run in this container; the `derivationInputs` docblock quotes about 14 s cold for a discovery. I have no before-number and did not take one. State the before and after for one cold `--commands` run in the PR body.

Not covered, checked, no live instance found (nits):

- N1 `createRequire` / `require('./x')`: not read. No first-party relative `require` under `scripts/pm/` at this head (the three hits are child-source strings requiring builtins or packages).
- N2 A template-literal specifier with an interpolation is counted as unread (so the file widens) but names nothing itself; a specifier table kept in a different file than the `import()` is not followed; a `from` followed by a newline before the specifier is missed by the inherited regex. No live instance of any of the three under `scripts/`.
- N3 The transitive evidence is fixture-only: both live replay chains are one level deep (`execute.mjs` imports `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` directly, `validate.mjs` imports `check-governed-merges.mjs` directly).
- N4 The measured figures (24 modules, 1003 pairs, about 42 families, 52 for `clause2-line.mjs`) and the "266 of 443" in the `derivationInputs` docblock are pinned by no row and will drift; not re-measured here.

### ② Semver level

No published package is touched: both files are under `scripts/pm/`. `skip-changeset` is on the PR and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. `Clause-②: no` is on the PR body and on the claim, and is right: no schema, no published surface, no narrowing of a declared capability. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No semver level is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **File surface.** The diff is exactly the two claimed files. No breach.
- **Deviation 1 (an ablation on a script).** Accepted as a one-off on disk with the restore evidence quoted (blob equals HEAD, empty `git diff HEAD`). Whether the order asked for it is the seat's to confirm; I did not read the order.
- **Deviation 2 (ablation on `e6452d31`, before `main` was merged).** Answered above: the ablated blob is this head's blob. Accepted.
- **Deviation 3 (`pnpm check:i18n-coverage` exit 3 locally).** The dev's reading is right. The script is `--self-test && scan`, so an exit 3 from the pair means the self-test half exited 0; 3 is `EXIT_PREREQUISITE_NOT_MET` (the CLI build closure was absent), not a finding. The family is derived only because its self-test imports the engine (`import('./pm/dispatch-gates.mjs')`, line 1475), and that half ran. CI covers the scan half: the step `Check no new untranslated declared labels` in `Type Check · consumer gates` runs `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` after the build, and it concluded success on this head.
- **Open question (cost: most pm edits now name about 42 families, 62 commands).** Answer: A, keep it transitive, unbounded. Options B (one level) and C (a fan-in cap) both cut real load chains and so fail toward deriving LESS, which is the defect being fixed; the list is run through `--commands` and reconciled by `--ran`, not read by eye, and each added row prints its chain. If the volume is to come down, the place is the load cycle among the pm modules, not the key. Not escalated; S2 asks for the wall-clock half of the price.
- **Out-of-scope finding (`check:adr-anchors` under-declares its population).** Escalated to the seat: the dev filed it with `carrier: none`, and a note in a PR body is not a carrier. Suggested carrier: one new `finding` card, filing gate ①, `domain:skills`, on `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` (declare the whole-tree population its scan reads), citing PR #33975 as the measurement. Read here only as far as this: that script carries no `dispatch-gates:` declaration at this head; the five-hint count is the dev's and was not re-derived.
- **Serial note (#34002, same file).** Held, not folded in. Correct.

### ④ Design judgment

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — the design holds against the card's scenario: scoping the key to `scripts/pm/` keeps the #13126 refusal where its price was measured, placing it last makes it additive without a row having to argue it, and printing the chain makes each added lead checkable. The load-edge reader is a separate function from `firstPartyImportBindings` for a stated reason (a population question against a load question) and reuses its regexes and its resolution rule. Where it does not hold is M1: the one place the reader narrows (root-spelled literals under an unread `import()`) rests on a statement about the tree that the tree contradicts, in the family the card names.

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` — the rows agree with the code they pin, and the two forced edits keep their rows' claims. The row asserting that a root-spelled path is not an edge pins the behaviour M1 asks to change.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8x8llj`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmPd7uRqHauEehGPr19`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b8685e50db4d8da9e5b10e9737d6547c71c62735`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` + none

Delta round against the FAIL record 6898932707 on `80bc14b0`. Inputs read: the delta `80bc14b0..b8685e50` (two commits, `6f34ab17` and `b8685e50`, no merge; the same two files, +64 / -19), the net diff against `main` (merge base `e71ecc1b`, 2 files, +395 / -10), the current PR body, the round-2 os-dev-report 6899446197 on card #33848, and the check-runs on this head. No local run: the new live row is executed by `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, which is green on this head, so the probe was not needed.

Check-runs on the head: nothing is still running. Every Lint lane (`Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, the other five and the `Lint & Repo Gates` aggregator), all four Type Check lanes, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` (both runs), `Test Core` and `Test UI` completed success. `Check Changeset` is skipped on this head (the `skip-changeset` label is on the PR). `mergeable_state` reads `clean`.

Findings on this head: 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix, 4 nits.

### ① Derived judgments

**M1 — closed.** The fallback under an unreadable `import()` now also admits a code-position module literal spelled from the repo root under `scripts/`: `LOAD_MODULE_LITERAL` gains the `scripts/` alternative and the loop sends such a literal to `admit` directly. The docblock sentence that the tree contradicted is replaced by one naming both in-process sites I cited (`fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`'s sender roster, `check-dispatch-gates.mjs`'s `import(resolve(ROOT, TOOL))`), and it states the over-derivation it accepts (the five modules `check-governed-merges.mjs` names as data). The PR body carries the same correction. A live-tree row pins `scripts/pm/issue-create.mjs` placing `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch` with a `via` that starts `import graph`; the fixture widen row now expects both spellings and its CONTROL carries both literals in a file with no unread `import()`. The dev reports an ablation of the root-spelled admission turning exactly those two rows red of 2215; not re-run here, and the lane that runs both rows is green on this head.

**The admission cannot narrow, and it fails toward more.** Checked by reading:

- The regex change is a pure alternation added in front of the same tail. A literal that matched before starts with `./` or `../` and still matches the first alternative; a root-spelled match contains no quote character, so it cannot swallow the opening of a relative literal that matched before.
- The only new statement is an `admit` call, which adds to the target set under the same guards as before (inside `scripts/`, outside `node_modules`, not the file itself, target exists). Nothing is removed from any file's targets.
- So every family's `importReach` is a superset of what it was on `80bc14b0`, and the key that reads it is still the last statement of `coveringKey`: every pair an earlier key answered keeps its key and label, every pair the import graph answered before is still answered, and `derivationInputs` only grows.
- A file with no unread `import()` is untouched (the CONTROL row pins it), so the widening stays confined to files whose load set the scan already admits it cannot read.

**S2 — closed.** The `derivationInputs` docblock and the PR body now state two cold readings each side: a discovery 16.6 s and 14.8 s before against 17.2 s and 17.0 s after; a whole `--commands` run 36.0 s and 37.0 s before against 38.0 s and 35.7 s after, with my 48.7 s named as a loaded-box reading. The dev's numbers, not re-measured; the delta they show is within their own run-to-run spread, which is an acceptable price.

**S1 — closed by carrier.** The spawned-child closure is carried by #34084 (open, `domain:skills`, `priority:p3`, `pm:queue`, titled for exactly this gap), and the PR body's not-covered note now names the closure rather than only the spawned file and cites that carrier. I agree with carrying it: no live miss was shown in round 1, and the root-spelled admission incidentally closes the one live instance I named, since `check-dispatch-gates.mjs` now reaches `dispatch-gates.mjs` and its closure through its own unread `import()`.

Round-1 nits: N4 is closed (a self-test row prints modules reached, pairs and the most-reached module on every run; the report reads 28 modules, 1195 pairs, 53 families for `clause2-line.mjs`, up from 24 / 1003 / 52, which is the root-spelled widening and the expected direction). N1, N2 and N3 stand as nits. New nits:

- N5 The docblock line under the fallback still reads "Resolution is … relative specifiers only"; with the root spelling admitted that sentence is one clause short.
- N6 The root-spelled admission reads whole literals only. A path assembled from segments (`join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'pm', 'x.mjs')`), or a sender the dispatcher's battery discovers at run time that is not in its `KNOWN` floor, is still named by nothing. No live instance of the first; the second is a new file's first card. #34084 is a reasonable place to note both.
- N7 The round-2 report's `line_budget` still reads +347 / -7; the net diff is +395 / -10. No ratcheted surface is touched either way.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from round 1. Both files are under `scripts/pm/`, no published package is touched, `skip-changeset` is on the PR, `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the body and are right. No semver level is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **File surface.** The delta and the net diff are exactly the two claimed files. No breach.
- **Deviations 1 to 3.** Answered in the round-1 record; nothing in the delta changes them. The round-2 ablation is reported on blob `8e00e6752a69`, which is the blob of `dispatch-gates.mjs` at this head (the delta's index line reads `7d65b7fe..8e00e675`).
- **Deviation 4 (the dev did not patch the PR body; the seat did).** Accepted: the body on the PR at review time carries the round-2 text, including both carriers.
- **Open question (cost).** Answered A in round 1; the report now lists none open. The measured time price above supports that answer.
- **Out-of-scope finding (`check:adr-anchors`).** Carried by #34086 (open, `finding`) and named in the PR body. Escalation answered. That card has no domain or priority label yet; that is triage's.
- **Serial note (#34002).** Still held, not folded in.

### ④ Design judgment

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — the one narrowing that rested on a false statement about the tree is gone, and the reader now errs toward more at every point where it cannot read a load: static and literal edges are read, an unreadable `import()` takes every first-party module literal the file spells. What remains uncovered (spawned-child closures, segment-assembled paths, `require`) is named, has no shown live miss, and has a carrier. The design holds against the card's scenario and against the dispatcher case round 1 raised.

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` — the row that pinned the old behaviour is rewritten to pin the new one together with its control, and the live sender row asserts the family, the verdict and the key that carried it. The price row asserts only non-emptiness and prints the rest, which is the right shape for a number that moves with the tree.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8x8llj`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmPd7uRqHauEehGPr19`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · head `b8685e50db4d8da9e5b10e9737d6547c71c62735` · 2026-11-15T18:51Z

- **形态:** 2 files, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` and `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` (+395/−10). `check-governed-merges --pr 34080`: NOT governed.
- **前提实测:** on main `a3aa1d29`, `--commands` over the queue guard and check-governed-merges derived 35 commands and none named `check:pm-fleet-write-execute`; ten `scripts/pm` files import `check-governed-merges.mjs`. A new import-graph key, consulted last in `coveringKey`, now derives every family whose gate files load a changed `scripts/pm/**` module, transitively; the #33804 replay derives 62 commands including the three fleet-write families.
- **复核:** FAIL 6898932707 on `80bc14b0` (M1: a root-spelled target under an unreadable `import()` dropped, toward deriving less; S1 spawned-child closures; S2 wall-clock price unstated); delta PASS 6899481531 on this head, `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, M1 and S2 closed, S1 closed by carrier #34084; no must-fix, no should-fix open. The root-spelled admission only adds targets, so no family derives less than before.
- **门禁 check-runs:** 48 on this head, all completed, 26 success, 22 skipped, none red.
- **接受的偏差:** nits N1–N3 (no `require`, no interpolated or cross-file specifiers, transitive evidence fixture-only; no live instance of any), N5 (one docblock clause short), N6 (segment-assembled paths, noted for #34084), N7 (the round-2 report's line count is stale). Cost question answered: keep the reach transitive and unbounded (about 53 families for a typical pm edit; discovery 17 s cold, measured before and after).
- **范围外去向:** spawned-child closures → #34084; `check:adr-anchors` population under-declared → #34086.
- **落地:** K = 2 (PRBASE `63db7240`). Not governed → ready + auto-merge by this seat.
